Alex (Acme Integrations): hey @Maya :wave: we're trying to do live reranking — stream candidate scores as they come in — against /v1/rerank but keep getting a 415. reproducer below. Is rerank supposed to accept SSE?

Maya - support: hey Alex — can you paste the exact curl and the body you're sending? 415 usually means content-type mismatch.

Alex (Acme Integrations): sure, here's what our streaming lib sends (we used same code as for generation):

```bash
curl -N -i \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank\" \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: text/event-stream\" \n  --data-binary $'event: candidate\\n\\ndata: {"candidate":"Option A"}\\n\\n'
```

Response is: `HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type` with body `{"error":"unsupported content type: text/event-stream","request_id":"req_abc123","status":415}`

Maya - support: thanks — that error matches a client trying to open an SSE stream. The rerank endpoint does not support streaming input or SSE. It expects a single request with content-type `application/json`. If you're chunking candidate events, the platform rejects it. Can you try a simple JSON request?

Alex (Acme Integrations): yeah we assumed rerank worked like generation streaming. our use-case is low-latency per-candidate scoring so we attempted streaming each candidate as it arrives. sample fixed request?

rachel-eng: hi — tagging in for engineering context. Quick note: rerank is synchronous. Accepts one payload: query + list of candidates (array) or ndjson depending on the path; streaming isn't supported and will surface 415 or 413 depending on headers. If you send chunked SSE the server sees `text/event-stream` and rejects. For repro we saw two failure modes: (1) 415 Unsupported Media Type when Content-Type != application/json, (2) 413 Payload Too Large when trying to send a very large chunked body per candidate with Transfer-Encoding: chunked plus no content-type.

Maya - support: can you try this minimal curl and confirm?

```bash
curl -i \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank\" \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"query":"Which option is clearer?","candidates":["Option A","Option B","Option C"]}'
```

rachel-eng: expected good response:

```json
{"request_id":"req_def456","scores":[{"candidate":"Option A","score":0.82},{"candidate":"Option B","score":0.12},{"candidate":"Option C","score":0.06}],"status":200}
```

Alex (Acme Integrations): ok that works when we send all candidates in one shot. but our microservice pipeline produces candidates lazily. any recommendations for streaming-friendly pattern?

rachel-eng: two options: (a) buffer small batches on your side (e.g., batch every 10 candidates or 100ms) and call rerank with an array — this is usually best for cost/latency tradeoff; (b) keep a lightweight local scorer for prefiltering and use rerank for final top-K. We don't have SSE for rerank today. We're tracking a feature request but no ETA.

Maya - support: also note limits — max candidates per request is 100 (documented). If you send >100 you'll see a 400 with message `too many candidates`. If you attempt to stream each candidate as its own HTTP request, you'll get billed per request; Sam from billing can advise about credits if their test traffic generated unexpected charges. :money_with_wings:

Sam - billing: hi Alex — I can review the request IDs. I see `req_abc123` and a few others in our logs around the same timeframe. If these were accidental test traffic caused by the streaming attempt, we can issue a 1x credit for the test window. Please DM me the org id or paste the last 5 digits of the invoice so I can attach a note.

Alex (Acme Integrations): thanks Sam — I'll DM invoice #INV-4521. also fwiw we got weird scores while experimenting where all candidates returned the exact same score — was that related to streaming?

rachel-eng: equal scores usually mean either (1) model fallback / error path where scoring failed and we returned default uniform scores, or (2) you hit a rate-limited/degenerate model variant because of routing. Can you paste the failing request_id(s)? fallback responses usually include a `variant` field. When you tried the streaming curl we saw `req_abc123` which returned the 415 — that one didn't produce scores. For the equal-score case, send the request body and the request_id from the successful 200 responses.

Alex (Acme Integrations): here's one request that returned weird uniform scores: `req_uniform789` with body `{"query":"Which UX is clearer?","candidates":["A","B","C","D"]}`

rachel-eng: thanks — we'll pull logs for `req_uniform789`. Maya, can you escalate to infra with those IDs? I'll check model routing and whether any fallback occurred.

Maya - support: escalated to eng-infra — adding links to logs and the customer reproducer. @rachel-eng please advise if we should temporarily whitelist their org for a small test to avoid rate-based fallbacks.

rachel-eng: doing that now. quick fix we pushed for the customer: (1) change Content-Type: application/json, (2) batch candidates to <= 50 per call, (3) include `prefer_model_variant` header if you need a stable variant.

Alex (Acme Integrations): confirmed — switching to batch-by-50 fixed both the 415 and the uniform-score problem (looks like a routing fallback was being hit when they sent a flood of tiny requests). Thanks everyone :relieved:

Maya - support: perfect. We're leaving the thread open until Sam confirms the billing credit and eng confirms logs. If you'd like, we can send a short how-to doc for batching patterns.

Sam - billing: credit queued for review — will confirm in DM.

rachel-eng: follow-ups for product/infra: log clearer 415 message suggesting \"Content-Type: application/json required\" and add doc note that rerank does not support SSE. Filing internal ticket RT-9981.

Alex (Acme Integrations): awesome, thanks all. saved my day.
